proposals.evidence: DEDR4641 documents Tamil mañcu and Kota manj cloud, and Malayalam maññu/Kannada mañju mist or fog. These survey mañj-/mañc- cloud responses extend that documented family comparatively to minority lects. Palatal/affricate spellings and final vowels are preserved; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review, and no literal DEDR attestation is claimed for absent lects. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4888 gives Malayalam mukaḷ ‘top, ridge, roof’, Kannada mogaḷu/mogaḍu ‘ridge of roof’ and Tamil mukaṭu ‘top, ridge of roof’. The selected simple survey roof nouns are comparative extensions to this regional family, retaining lateral/stop and vowel differences; longer mukaḷ-kūrɛ compounds are excluded here. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR156(a) gives Tamil appaṉ, Malayalam appan, Kannada appa and Kodagu appë father. The selected survey appa/appan/appe responses retain the same locally elicited father sense; minority-lect extensions are comparative. This nursery/honorific family does not by itself distinguish shared inheritance from regional diffusion, and other languages’ mother/aunt senses are not substituted. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2248 gives Tamil/Malayalam kōḻi fowl, Kota kōy, Kodagu kōḷi, Kannada kōḻi and Tulu kōri/kōḷi. These southern survey kōyi/koyɨ/kōḷi/kośi/kojī-type responses are comparative lect extensions, retaining the glide, lateral and palatal/sibilant variants. The source chicken sense is compatible with fowl; this does not merge them with the distinct central-Dravidian kor family. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
